title: Detecting and Mitigating Subliminal Bias Transmission in LLM Distillation
summary: This paper proposes a method to detect and mitigate the transmission of behavioral traits (e.g., biases) through subliminal learning during LLM distillation. We introduce a framework that identifies hidden signals in synthetic data generated by teacher models and applies counteractive constraints during student model training. The approach is validated by measuring bias amplification in downstream tasks using datasets with known bias baselines, comparing models trained with and without the proposed mitigation.
gap: While subliminal learning has been observed in controlled settings, its impact on bias transmission during distillation remains unmeasured, especially in real-world applications where synthetic data is widely used.
approach: We develop a two-stage process: (1) a statistical analysis of synthetic data to detect hidden signals correlated with known biases, and (2) a constrained optimization technique during student model training that penalizes the reproduction of these signals. The method leverages mechanistic interpretability to identify neuron populations responsible for bias transmission.
evaluation: We evaluate using the RealToxicityPrompts dataset and political bias benchmarks, comparing bias scores (e.g., toxicity, political leaning) of student models trained with/without mitigation. Baselines include standard distillation and adversarial training. Success is measured by reduced bias amplification while maintaining task performance.
